description: Not needed as separate types; skipped.
acceptance: Exports a Viewport union type 'mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop'
Exports the breakpoint boundaries (640 and 1024) as named constants so the hook and any consumer share one definition

description: Hook that reports which of the three viewport bands the window currently falls into, updating on resize.
acceptance: Returns 'mobile' for widths of 640px or less
Returns 'tablet' for widths between 641px and 1023px inclusive
Returns 'desktop' for widths of 1024px or more
Subscribes to viewport width changes and re-reports when the band changes, cleaning up its listener on unmount

description: Reusable data-access hook wrapping the existing GET_CARS query and ADD_CAR mutation, exposing cars, loading, error and an addCar function that makes the new vehicle appear without a reload.
acceptance: Imports GET_CARS and ADD_CAR from src/graphql/queries.ts rather than declaring new documents
Returns { cars: Car[]; loading: boolean; error?: unknown; addCar }
Fetches the inventory when first used
addCar(make, model, year, color) runs the ADD_CAR mutation and updates the cached inventory so the new vehicle is included in the returned cars without a refetch of the page
Is the only module in the project that issues GraphQL operations for the inventory

description: Pure helpers for narrowing the inventory by model text and ordering it by year or by make, composable so sorting applies to an already filtered list.
acceptance: Exports filterByModel(cars, query) matching partial, case-insensitive model text and returning all cars for an empty query
Exports sortCars(cars, key) supporting 'year' and 'make'
Both functions return new arrays and do not mutate their input
Composing filter then sort preserves the filter

description: Presentational card for one vehicle showing make, model, year, colour and the photograph appropriate to the current viewport band, built with the project's existing component library.
acceptance: Takes a single Car as prop and issues no GraphQL query of its own
Renders make, model, year and colour as text
Renders the car's mobile image on mobile, tablet image on tablet and desktop image on desktop, chosen via useViewport
Image has meaningful alt text identifying the vehicle
Uses the component library the project already depends on rather than a new one

description: Responsive grid that renders a CarCard for each vehicle passed to it and shows a plain empty state when the list is empty.
acceptance: Takes cars: Car[] as prop and renders one CarCard per vehicle, keyed by id
Lays cards out in a grid that reflows to fewer columns as the screen narrows
Issues no GraphQL query of its own
Renders a short empty-state message when given zero cars

description: Controlled text input for filtering the inventory by model name as the user types.
acceptance: Takes value and onChange props and calls onChange on every keystroke
Has an accessible label identifying it as a model search
Holds no inventory state and issues no GraphQL query

description: Control that lets the user choose to sort the inventory by year or by make.
acceptance: Takes the current sort key and an onChange prop
Offers exactly the options 'year' and 'make', each with a visible label
Has an accessible label identifying it as the sort control
Issues no GraphQL query

description: Form collecting make, model, year and colour and submitting a new vehicle through the addCar callback it is given.
acceptance: Renders labelled fields for make, model, year and colour plus a submit control
Calls the onAdd prop with the entered values on submit
Rejects submission when any required field is empty and surfaces a visible validation message instead of calling onAdd
Clears the fields after a successful submission
Issues no GraphQL operation itself; it receives the add callback as a prop

description: Container screen that reads inventory through useCars, holds filter and sort state, and composes the filter input, sort control, add form and card list, plus loading and error messaging.
acceptance: Shows a visible loading indicator while the inventory request is in flight
Shows a plain error message, not an empty inventory, when the request fails
Passes filterByModel then sortCars output to CarList so sorting keeps the filter applied
Wires AddCarForm's submission to the addCar function from useCars so the new vehicle appears in the list without a reload
Contains no GraphQL documents of its own

description: Application entry component wiring the Apollo client provider around the Inventory screen.
acceptance: Wraps the tree in ApolloProvider using the existing client from src/graphql/client.ts
Renders the Inventory screen
Contains no presentation markup for vehicles and no data access of its own

description: Test helper that renders a component inside the Apollo provider used by the app, so tests exercise the project's mock API.
acceptance: Exports renderWithProviders(ui) wrapping the ui in ApolloProvider with the project's client
Sets up a fresh Apollo cache per render so tests do not leak data between each other
Re-exports Testing Library queries and userEvent for convenience

description: Test that the inventory renders once data arrives from the mock API, and that loading and error states are shown appropriately.
acceptance: Renders Inventory via renderWithProviders and asserts a loading indicator appears first
Asserts every seeded vehicle's make and model is on screen after the query resolves
Asserts an error message, and no empty inventory, is shown when the mock API is made to fail for the cars query
Runs against the existing MSW mock API, never a live network

description: Test that typing part of a model name narrows the rendered inventory.
acceptance: Waits for the seeded inventory to render, then types partial model text into the model filter
Asserts matching vehicles remain on screen and non-matching ones are removed
Asserts clearing the input restores the full list
Runs against the existing MSW mock API

description: Test that choosing a sort option reorders the inventory and that sorting a filtered list keeps the filter applied.
acceptance: Asserts card order changes to ascending year when sorting by year
Asserts card order changes when sorting by make
Filters by model first, then sorts, and asserts the filtered subset stays filtered in the new order
Runs against the existing MSW mock API

description: Test that submitting the add form creates a vehicle through the mutation and shows it in the list without a reload, and that empty submissions are rejected.
acceptance: Fills make, model, year and colour and submits, then asserts the new vehicle appears in the inventory list without re-rendering the app
Asserts submitting with empty fields shows a validation message and adds nothing to the list
Runs the ADD_CAR mutation against the existing MSW mock API
